content:
If you're anything like me, you've definitely spent way too much time on Wikipedia, clicking around reading random articles. Now there's finally an official app—no, should say, widget—for you to do just that.

Finally, there's a button that can directly open a random Wikipedia article

Today's update to the Wikipedia iOS app added a fun and practical new feature: a "Random Article" widget that can be placed on the iPhone and iPad home screen.

It comes in two sizes (large and medium), and also has a cute mascot.

Tap the widget and it'll take you to a completely random Wikipedia article, and also turn on Random mode for you.

No need to leave the app and tap the widget again. Just press the random button, and it'll keep taking you deeper into this random maze, like rolling dice.

Have fun, but be careful not to lose track of time! Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app also added a history trivia mini-game.

After you update your Wikipedia iPhone and iPad app today, you can find this new widget.
